newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes rise sharply in Asia on Iraq, Oman firms.
newsitem.headline: Crudes rise sharply in Asia on Iraq, Oman firms.

text.p: Crude oil prices rose sharply in Asia on Monday following a decision by the United Nations to delay limited oil sales by Iraq after Baghdad sent troops into Kurdish areas in the north of the country, traders said.
U.N. relief officials and guards said on Monday that Iraqi troops had evacuated the Iraqi Kurdistan capital of Arbil which they captured on Saturday.
At 0810 GMT, October cash Brent was notionally assessed at $21.40/21.50, against late Friday U.S. levels of $20.80/20.85.
Brent/Dubai spreads were scarce but were assessed wider in line with rising Brent and weaker Dubai values, brokers said.
October and November Brent/Dubai were both bid at $1.75 with no offers, brokers said.
October/November Dubai was nominally assessed at 40/50 cents, against late Friday U.S. levels of 48/55 cents.

Dubai was seen weaker because the IOC shunned offers for the crude while taking three VLCCs of Qua Iboe, one VLCC of Suez Blend as well as 600,000 barrels of Malaysia Labuan in its tender, traders said. In addition to the estimated three Dubais left unsold, two majors are mulling whether to sell their cargoes, they said. Buyers are seen targetting a price of about full month quotes plus 50 cents, they added.
